~ א.

כשרואה אדם, שיש לו עקמימות בלבו, בפרט כשיש לו, חס ושלום, עקמימות הרבה בלבו, אזי הוא צריך לשום עצמו כבהמה ולסלק דעתו לגמרי כאלו אין לו שום דעת כלל ולסמך רק על אמונה וילך רק בתמימות ובפשיטות לבד, ואזי זוכה אחר כך לדעת גדול מאד בחינת מחין של תפלין. (הלכות תפלין, הלכה ד', אות ו):

~ ב.

כל העקמימות שיש בלב הרבה בני אדם, שאומרים, שאינם יכולים לעסק בעבודת השם מחמת חסרון פרנסה ושאר יסורין ומניעות, חס ושלום, כל זה נמשך מבחינת המבוכה של הקושיא של צדיק ורע לו רשע וטוב לו, שזאת המבוכה מבלבל הרבה בני אדם, ואפלו מי שאינו נכנס כלל במחשבתו בקושיא זאת, אוף על פי כן כל כל הדבורים הנ"ל, הכל נמשך ונשתלשל משם, ועקר התקון לזה הוא רק תמימות ופשיטות, להשליך כל החכמות ולבלי להרהר אחריו יתברך כלל ולידע ולהאמין ולהאמין כי ישרים דרכי השם ולהתגבר בכל מה שעובר עליו לחטף בכל יום איזה טוב כל מה שיוכל, כי לית יום דלית בה טוב, ולא יהרהר על משפטיו יתברך כלל, שזה עקר האמונה - להאמין שהכל מהשם יתברך ואין להרהר אחריו כלל, כי צדיק וישר הוא, ובזה בעצמו ממתיקין הדינים וזוכין להתקרב להתקרב להשם יתברך דיקא על ידי כל זה שעובר עליו. (הלכות ראש חדש, הלכה ו', אות יב):

~ ג.

צריך כל אחד להסתכל בנפשו, שלא יצא מדרכי התמימות באמת, ולחפש דרכיו בכל עת, ולשמר נפשו מאד, שלא יטה אותו הבעל דבר מן האמת, חס ושלום, על ידי חכמות של הבל, המצויים עתה בעוונותינו הרבים, ושלא יהפך לו אמת לשקר ועברה למצוה, חס ושלום, כי זה גרוע מן הכל, חס ושלום, ויזכר את עצמו בכל עת איך שאינו נקי בענין תאות משגל, ועל ידי זה כלי כלי המחין שלו אינם בשלמות, ואפלו אם הוא מוחזק ומפורסם ללמדן גדול וחסיד, אוף על פי כן מאחר שיודע בנפשו, שאינו נקי וזך בענין זה בשלמות כראוי, וממילא תפיסת המחין שלו אינם בשלמות, על כן תכף כשרוצה הבעל דבר להטותו מדרך התמימות האמתי אפלו נקודה בעלמא, ואף על פי שנדמה לו שעל פי התורה מגיע כך, צריך לירא לנפשו ולחשב אולי אולי טועה הוא בדבר ומחשבה זו וסברא זאת נמשך אצלו מבחינת: לא זכה - נעשית לו סם מות, רחמנא לצלן, שנאמר על מי שלא זכה עדין לשלמות כלי המחין על ידי תקון הברית בשלמות, על כן הוא הוא צריך לזהר ביותר שלא להטעות את עצמו ושלא להפך דברי אלקים חיים, חס ושלום, וביותר ויותר צריך לזהר בענין זה לענין מחלקת, כאשר כבר ראינו כמה נפשות שירדו חיים שאולה, רחמנא לצלן, על ידי שהרבו במחלקת על הכשרים מחמת טעות דעתם ושנדמה להם כאלו כונתם לשם שמים, וכמבאר בפנים. וגם לענין עצמו לבד בעבודת השם, צריכין גם כן לצעק ולזעק הרבה להשם יתברך, שיוליכהו בדרך הישר והאמת תמיד, אולי יזכה להתקרב להשם יתברך כראוי, וכאשר צעק דוד המלך הרבה על זה, כמבאר בפנים, כי צריכין לזכות גדול וישועה גדולה ורחמים גדולים והשתדלות ויגיעה גדולה כל ימי חייו, שיזכה לפלס דרכיו באמת בכל עת ולילך בדרך הקדש באמת לאמתו ולא יטה לימין ולשמאל ולא יטעה את עצמו באיזה דבר, חס ושלום, על ידי שאין הכלים של המחין שלו שלמים כראוי, אבל על כל פנים כששומר את עצמו שלא יהיה נוטה על כל פנים מדרכי התמימות, אזי הוא בטוח על כל פנים ממכשול גמור, חס ושלום, כי הולך בתם ילך בטח. (הלכות יין נסך, הלכה ד', אות יג, טז, יז):

~ ד.

כל מי שמרגיש בעצמו, שאינו קדוש כראוי, צריך להכניע ולבטל עצמו נגד השם יתברך ולא ירצה לילך בגדולות ובנפלאות ממנו להמשיך על עצמו בחינת רוח הקדש, רוח נבואה, מאחר שיודע שרחוק מזה, ואם ירצה להמשיך על עצמו בחינת מראות וחזיונות, יוכל לקלקל יותר ויותר, כאשר נכשלו בזה רבים מאד, רק צריך שילך בתמימות ולבקש מהשם יתברך, שיהיה בעזרו לצאת מפחיתותו ויזכה לקדש את עצמו כראוי, ואז - אם יזכה ויהיה ראוי לזה לקבל רוח הקדש, דרך הקדושה, בשלמות - השם הטוב יעשה עמו כרצונו. (הלכות חדש, הלכה ד', אות ח):

~ ה.

באמת אין לך אדם שאין לו שעה, אך הרבה אובדים השעה שלהם, שהיה יכול להצליח בה בגשמיות וברוחניות, על ידי חכמתם של הבל, על ידי שדוחקים את השעה, כמו שאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה: כל הדוחק את השעה, השעה דוחקתו, כי השם יתברך מקים: עם גבר תמים תתמם ועם עקש תתפתל, ומאחר שהוא עקש ורוצה שימלא לו השם יתברך תכף חפצו, וכשאין לו מה שחפץ הוא אומר, שאי אפשר בזה האפן לעבד את השם יתברך נמצא, שהוא עקש ומהרהר אחר מדותיו יתברך, ואז גם השם יתברך מתפתל עמו והשעה דוחקתו אבל ההולך בתמימות ומאמין באמת כי בודאי צדיק וישר השם, ומה שסובל יסורין ודחקות - הכל לטובה, כי עדין לא הגיעה השעה שלו, ומקים: טוב ויחיל ודומם לתשועת השם, כי לפעמים אין השם יתברך נותן להאדם צרכי ישועתו תכף, עד שירבה בתפלה על זה, כי השם יתברך מתאוה לתפלתן של ישראל], וגם בתפלה אסור לדחק את השעה, כמבאר במקום אחר, ולפעמים הישועה מתעכבת עוד מטעמים אחרים, על כן צריכין לילך רק בתמימות ולהאמין בישר משפטיו יתברך ולהרבות בתפלה תמיד על כל דבר, ואז בודאי השעה עומדת לו, כי בודאי תגיע השעה של ישועתו. וכן מבאר בדברי חכמינו זכרונם לברכה: כל המתמים עצמו, שעה עומדת לו וכו'. (הלכות נזיקין, הלכה ה', אות טו):

~ ו.

מי שהולך בתמימות, הוא עקר הבן החביב להשם יתברך, כמבאר בפנים, ומי שהולך אחר החכמות והערמימיות של הבל, שהם כמו בחינת נחושים ממש, רחמנא לצלן, הוא בחינת עקש ופתלתל, והשם יתברך מקים עמו: עם עקש תתפתל, והוא בחינת בעל מום, שהוא ההפך מתמימות, שהוא לשון שלמות. (שם, אות טז):

~ ז.

עקר מה שהשם יתברך מתפאר עם ישראל נגד כל האומות הוא על ידי דרכי התמימות שלהם האמתיים, וזה בחינת: ששים המה מלכות וכו', אחת היא יונתי תמתי - תמתי דיקא, בחינת תמימות. (שם, אות כב):

תם ונשלם. שבח לאל בורא עולם:

סליק ספר עצות ישרות בעזרת רוכב שמים ומסדר המערכות:
segments.en: All the crookedness in the heart of many people — who say that they are unable to engage in the service of G-d because of deficiency of livelihood and other sufferings and obstacles, G-d forbid — all of this derives from the aspect of the confusion of the question of tzadik v'ra lo, rasha v'tov lo [why the righteous suffer and the wicked prosper]. For this confusion confuses many people. And even one who does not enter this question into his thought at all — even so, all of — [all of] — the aforementioned words derive and flow from there. And the essential repair for this is only temimus and simplicity: to cast aside all the wisdoms — and not to contemplate at all regarding His ways, blessed be He. And to know and believe — and believe — that "the ways of G-d are straight" [Hosea 14:10]. And to overpower oneself in all that passes over him — to seize some good each day — as much as possible. For lais yoma d'lais bei tava [there is no day that does not have good in it]. And to not deliberate at all regarding His blessed judgments. For this is the essential faith: to believe that everything is from G-d — and not to contemplate at all regarding Him. For He is righteous and upright. And through this itself one sweetens the judgments. And merits to draw close — [to draw close] — to G-d specifically through all that passes over him.

Every person must look into his own soul — that he not depart from the ways of true temimus. And to search his ways at all times. And to guard his soul very much — that the baal davar should not divert him from the truth, G-d forbid, through the futile wisdoms that are so common now in our many sins. And that he not invert truth to falsehood and transgression to commandment for him, G-d forbid. For this is the worst of all, G-d forbid. And he should remind himself at all times — that he is not pure in the matter of the desire for sexual union. And through this — the vessels — [the vessels] — of his brain are not in perfection. And even if he is established and known as a great scholar and pious person — even so, since he knows within his own soul that he is not pure and clear in this matter in full perfection as is proper — and therefore his grasp of the mind is not in perfection — therefore immediately when the baal davar wishes to divert him from the path of true temimus even by a single point — even though it seems to him that the Torah mandates such — he must fear for his soul and consider: perhaps — [perhaps] — he is erring in the matter. And this thought and view derives in him from the aspect of: "if he has not merited — it becomes for him a deadly poison", G-d protect us — said of one who has not yet merited the perfection of the vessels of the brain through the repair of the bris in perfection. Therefore — he — [he] — must be especially careful not to mislead himself and not to invert the words of the living G-d, G-d forbid.

And he must be especially, especially careful in this matter regarding controversy. As we have already seen many souls who went down to the pit alive, G-d protect us, through having multiplied controversy against the upright because of the error of their mind — and it seemed to them that their intention was for the sake of Heaven. As is explained in the inner teachings. And also for himself alone in the service of G-d — one must also cry out and wail greatly to G-d, that He lead him in the straight and true path always. Perhaps he will merit to draw close to G-d as is proper. And as King David cried out much about this — as explained in the inner teachings. For one needs a very great merit and a very great salvation and very great compassion — and great striving and great toil all the days of his life — to merit to weigh out his ways in truth at every time and to walk in the holy path truly and truthfully and not deviate right or left. And not to mislead himself in any matter, G-d forbid — on account of the imperfection of the vessels of his brain. But at the very least — when one guards himself from deviating at the very least from the ways of temimus — then he is at least certainly protected from utter stumbling, G-d forbid. For "he who walks in wholeness walks securely" [Proverbs 10:9].

Every person who feels in himself that he is not holy as is proper — must humble and nullify himself before G-d. And not wish to go in matters too great and too wondrous for him [gedolos u'niflo'os mimenu] — to draw upon himself the aspect of the holy spirit, the spirit of prophecy. Since he knows that he is far from this. And if he wishes to draw upon himself the aspect of visions and sights — he can cause himself even more and more ruin. As very many have stumbled in this. Rather, he must go in temimus and beseech G-d to be in his aid — to emerge from his insignificance. And to merit to sanctify himself as is proper. And then — if he merits and is worthy of receiving the holy spirit, through the path of holiness, in perfection — G-d who is good will do with him as He wills.

In truth there is no person who does not have his hour [sha'ah]. But many lose their hour — in which they could have succeeded physically and spiritually — through their futile wisdoms. Through pressing the moment [dochek es hasha'ah]. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "Whoever presses the moment — the moment presses him." For G-d fulfills: "with the wholesome You act wholesomely, and with the crooked You act crookedly" [Psalms 18:27]. And since he is crooked and wishes G-d to immediately fulfill his desire — and when he does not have what he desires, he says that it is impossible in this way to serve G-d — it is thus found that he is crooked and deliberates regarding His blessed attributes. And then G-d also acts crookedly with him — and the moment presses him.

But one who goes in temimus and truly believes that G-d is certainly righteous and upright — and that the sufferings and hardship he endures are all for the good — for his hour has not yet come. And fulfills: "It is good to wait in silence for the salvation of G-d" [Lamentations 3:26]. For sometimes G-d does not give the person the needs of his salvation immediately — until he multiplies prayer about this. For "G-d longs for the prayer of Israel." And also in prayer it is forbidden to press the moment — as explained elsewhere. And sometimes the salvation is delayed still for other reasons. And therefore one must go only in temimus — and believe in the uprightness of His blessed judgments — and always multiply prayer for everything. And then certainly the moment stands [favorably] for him. For certainly the hour of his salvation will come. And as is explained in the words of our Sages of blessed memory: "Whoever makes himself whole [mistemim] — the moment stands favorably for him, etc."

One who goes in temimus — he is the essential beloved child before G-d, as explained in the inner teachings. And one who goes after the futile wisdoms and cunning schemes [armimiyos] of vanity — which are like actual divinations [nachushim mamash], G-d protect us — he is the aspect of crooked and twisted [ikaish u'fsaltal]. And G-d fulfills with him: "with the crooked You act crookedly" [Psalms 18:27]. And he is the aspect of one with a blemish [ba'al mum] — which is the opposite of wholeness [temimus] — which is the language of completeness [shleimus].

The essential [means by which] G-d takes glory in Israel before all the nations is through their true ways of temimus. And this is the aspect of: "There are sixty queens, etc. — one is she, my dove, my perfect one [tamasi]" [Song of Songs 6:8–9] — specifically tamasi — the aspect of temimus.
Completed and finished. Praise to G-d, Creator of the world.
Concluded: the book Aitzoas Yesharoas with the help of the Rider of the Heavens and the Arranger of the orders

It is a very severe prohibition to eat and drink before prayer — as explained in the holy Zohar. (Not as is common now, in our many sins, where people are lenient in this, especially regarding drinking coffee before prayer.) And many Tzaddikim were careful not to drink even water before prayer — even though it is technically permitted according to strict law. And through not eating before prayer — through this one draws the aspect of the repair drawn through a fast [ta'anis]. For this is also the aspect of a fast of hours [ta'anis sha'os]. And through this the speech is perfected — and one brings it out from the narrow passage of the throat. And one merits to speak complete words before G-d in his prayer. And through this the faith is completed — which is itself the aspect of prayer, as is known. Also through this one merits to begin each morning anew in the service of G-d — in the aspect of: "They are renewed each morning" [Lamentations 3:23].

Through sins, one causes, G-d forbid, the spirit of a person [ru'ach ho'odom] to become mingled with and exchanged for the spirit of an animal [ru'ach habeheimah]. This is the aspect of the exchange — that the prince's son was exchanged with the servant's son. And this is the secret of all the sacrifices [korbanos] — to extract the human spirit from the animal spirit. And each person — commensurate with how much he has mingled the human spirit with the animal spirit through his sins — when he does not merit to repair this during his lifetime, G-d forbid — then he must receive his punishment to be cast about within the hollow of a sling [kaf hakela] and to seek the sparks and the human spirit that he lost and cast into the animal spirit — until he receives his full punishment. And then he will be repaired. For the punishment is — [is] — for the sake of repair.

And through reciting the Torah portion of the sacrifices and the chapter Eizehu Mekoman, etc. — it is considered as if he offered sacrifices in those places. And through this he merits to extract the entire aspect of the human spirit from the animal spirit from all the places where they fell — [fell] — there. And to repair and elevate them from there. And this is the aspect of Pesukei d'Zimrah [the verses of song recited after this] — for the essential extraction of the human spirit from the animal spirit is through melody. Which is the aspect of the priests in their service and the Levites on their platform.

The entire matter of the prince's son who was exchanged with the servant's son — explained in the story-tales — encompasses the entire Torah entirely. And all that has passed from the beginning of the sin of Adam the first — who was expelled from the Garden of Eden, etc. — until the end: when our righteous Mashiach will come and the kingship will return to the true prince's son. And all the essential service of a person in this world is only in this matter — as explained in the inner teachings. And this is what the secret of the morning blessings and the sacrifices and Pesukei d'Zimrah and the Kriyas Shma and the Shemoneh Esreh — and the Shemoneh Esreh — revolves around, as explained in the inner teachings.

The essential joy of Israel is through faith — in the aspect of: "I will rejoice in G-d" [Habakkuk 3:18]. And this is the aspect of the Kriyas Shma — which is the foundation of faith. And since joy is a complete stature [komah sheleimah] with 248 limbs — therefore, after Shema Yisroel one reads the three Torah portions, etc. — which contain 248 words in the Kriyas Shma, as our Sages of blessed memory said. And through joy one merits redemption — in the aspect of: "For in joy you shall go forth" [Isaiah 55:12]. And this is the aspect of the blessing of redemption [bircas ge'ulah] recited after the Kriyas Shma. And one must juxtapose the redemption to the prayer. For the essential perfection of the service of prayer is when it is in joy — in the aspect of: "Serve G-d in joy" [Psalms 100:2]. And prayer is the aspect of attachment [devekus] to G-d, as is known — and this is the ultimate purpose of joy: to rejoice in Him, blessed be He, and to cling to Him in wondrous and extraordinary attachment.

And the essential construction of joy is through the ten types of melody. And therefore the essential prayer is with a quorum of ten [minyan]. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory said: "Any prayer that does not include among its worshipers [even] the sinners of Israel [is lacking], etc." [Kerisus 6b]. For this is the essential perfection of joy — to transform all kinds of sorrow and sighing into joy — so that they become a vehicle for holiness. And this is the aspect of the chelbenah [galbanum] in the incense [ketores]. For the incense is also the aspect of joy — in the aspect of: "incense gladdens the heart" [Proverbs 27:9]. And the chelbenah is the aspect of sorrow and sighing — which is also transformed into joy. And therefore every person must be careful to pray specifically with a congregation [tzibur] — so that even if he has some grip of sorrow and sighing — it too will be transformed into joy through the holiness of the large congregation. And therefore prayer is a healing for everything — for all healings come through joy.

All the alien thoughts and all the confusions — all of them — are the aspects of: arlas lev [foreskin of the heart], cherpos lev [shame of the heart], sheviras lev [breaking of the heart] — for they shame and disgrace and break a person's heart. And this is the essential service of prayer — to purify and cleanse the heart from all evil loves and from all desires and confusions — which are the aspect of cherpos lev, arlas lev as above — through the speech of prayer. Which is the aspect of tzadik moshel [the Tzadik who rules] — which is the aspect of the holy point where the light of holy love dwells. And therefore at the time of prayer all the confusions and all the alien thoughts intensify — as is the way of those fighting one another: when one side comes to nullify the other — the other wishes to overpower against it. Therefore in truth at the time of prayer it is a great battle. And one must be very careful to bind the speech of prayer — which is the aspect of the point aforementioned — to the heart. In order to nullify the cherpos lev aforementioned.

At the time of Minchah [the afternoon prayer] — then takfa d'dinah shalta [the force of strict judgment rules]. From which come all the obstacles from the service of G-d. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory warned especially not to delay the Minchah prayer — as is explained in the Mishnah: "A person should not sit before a barber, etc." Because the obstacles are most common then — since that is the time when most of the world is preoccupied with commerce and their livelihood. From which come all the obstacles from the service of G-d. And then a person must overpower himself more greatly with strong wills and great longings for G-d — in order to remember G-d within the commerce, within the intensity of the obstacles. And this is the essential [meaning]. And this is the aspect of the Minchah prayer. For prayer is the service of the heart — the aspect of ratzon [will]. But the essential intensification of the will is needed specifically at the time of Minchah. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory warned about it especially. For through the Minchah prayer one merits to draw the sweetening of the Minchah of Shabbos [minchah shel Shabbos] — when the essential illumination of the will — ra'ava d'ra'avin [the will of all wills] — shines, as is known. And because the holy will is the aspect of the minchas ani [offering of the poor] — therefore our Sages of blessed memory called this prayer by the name Minchah.

All day a person is preoccupied with his affairs and commerce — which is the aspect of sleep [shenah]. The Minchah prayer is where he remembers G-d and awakens from his sleep — which is the aspect of the commerce. And he pauses to pray Minchah. And therefore the Minchah prayer is the aspect of Rosh Hashanah — which is the aspect of the awakening of the year [his'orrus hashanah]. For Yitzchak established the Minchah prayer — which is the aspect of Rosh Hashanah, the fear of Yitzchak [pachad Yitzchok]. And therefore at that time the judgment is loosened [dina sharya]. And since the essential nourishment of the outer forces comes from the aspect of judgments — therefore they decreed that one should not begin to eat or work [at that time] — so as not to forget to pray. And our Sages of blessed memory said: "A person must always be diligent in the Minchah prayer" — for then extra vigilance is needed for the reason mentioned above.
The Minchah prayer with intention is a segula [-propitious means] for faith. And therefore Eliyahu merited to reveal the holy faith in the world at that time [minchah time].

Sometimes a person is in such smallness [katnus] that he cannot raise his voice at all. Even so, he must not despair of himself from prayer and supplication — and let him fulfill: "And you will be brought low from the earth you will speak… and from the dust your utterance will be chirped" [Isaiah 29:4]. Which is the aspect of: "From the depths I call You, G-d" [Psalms 130:1] — from depths of depths — the innermost of the heart — the aspect of: "Their heart cried out to G-d" [Lamentations 2:18]. Which is the aspect of the silent prayer [tefilah b'lochash] — which our Sages of blessed memory ordained for the smallest of the small. And also for the greatest of the great. For the very smallest — all their prayer is in the aspect of silent prayer as above. And their entire repair is through the great Tzaddikim — who also pray in a whisper [b'lochash]. For they ascend in their prayer to the aspect of Atikah [the Ancient One] — where the aspect of the whisper resides. The aspect of: "wise of hidden things and understanding of the whisper" [Isaiah 3:3]. For there is the aspect of: "a fence for wisdom is silence." And this is the aspect of: "Why do you cry out to Me?" [Exodus 14:15] — at Atikah the matter depends, as is explained in the holy Zohar. That is, for there at Atikah there is no crying out — only silence and a whisper. And this is the aspect of: "G-d will fight for you and you shall be silent" [Exodus 14:14]. For there in the time of katnus — one must cry out to G-d greatly. But in any case — for one must also strengthen himself even then in prayer and supplication — to pray in a whisper at least, from the depths of the heart — as mentioned above. And afterwards one merits to pray with a loud voice. Which is the aspect of the silent prayer — and afterwards the prayer leader [shali'ach tzibur] prays aloud.

Yaakov our Father, peace be upon him, through the greatness of his holiness, merited to lower himself to the very depth of the falls of all of Israel — in the general and the particular — and of every generation until the very footsteps of the Mashiach. And therefore he established the evening prayer [arvis] — which is at the time of complete darkness. For he illuminates the heart of Israel: that even in the utmost complete darkness one must also strengthen himself to engage in prayer. For lais re'usa tava d'is'avad [no good intention is ever lost]. And this he established at the time he merited to encounter the place — which is the place of the Temple. And there he merited to fully attain the very essence of the virtue of the awakening from below [is'arusa d'lisata]: that even any small awakening whatsoever — from whatever aspect and level it is — is never lost forever. For the true Tzadik — in the aspect of Yaakov — watches over this and gathers and collects everything and builds from it wondrous edifices. As all of this is explained in the inner teachings. And therefore he established the evening prayer — that even in the darkness of the night and actual gloom a person should awaken to pray and cry out to Him, blessed be He — in the aspect of: "From the belly of She'ol I cried out" [Jonah 2:3]. For even a cry from the lowest depths is never lost forever.

In truth — all that G-d does with a person is all for his benefit. As our Sages of blessed memory said: a person must say: "All that is done from Heaven — is done for good" [Berochois 60b]. If so, seemingly it is difficult: why did G-d command us to pray regarding the affliction, G-d protect us? For all the sufferings and afflictions, G-d forbid, are truly great goodnesses — to cause him to merit through them the life of eternity. But in truth — certainly all that G-d does with a person is all for the good. And even so, a person must pray and beseech G-d to emerge from the affliction to spaciousness. For the essential creation of the world was for the sake of the human being who has free will — that everything be delivered into the hands of the person. That is, the person specifically should make vessels and channels to draw down His bounty and kindness, blessed be He, below. And without the repair of the vessels — made by the person — the flow of kindness cannot descend below. For if the kindness were to descend before the repair of the vessels — it would be in the aspect of: "an abundance of oil causes the lamp to be extinguished." And then the kindness would be transformed into severe judgment, G-d forbid.

And the essential repair of the vessels is through Torah and prayer. And primarily through prayer. And therefore before a person prays — certainly everything that comes upon him is a great goodness, even sufferings, G-d forbid. For everything is for his benefit. For according to his deeds — no flow and vitality can descend to him except through this. And even this comes in great kindness. For if only kindness without any judgment at all were to flow to him — it would be, G-d forbid, in the aspect of an abundance of light that damages more. Therefore the essential repair is through prayer. For through prayer one sweetens the judgments and repairs vessels — in a manner that one can receive the flow of His blessed kindness without sufferings. Only through the repairs of the vessels that he repaired through prayer. And therefore the essential repair of prayer is through gazing at the purpose [tachlis] and including all the prayer in the One — where it is entirely good. As explained in the inner teachings. For without this — one cannot pray at all because of the aforementioned difficulty. As our Sages of blessed memory posed: "But does one give a child whatever he wants?" For since G-d knows the truth — that these sufferings from deficiency of livelihood and the like are for his eternal benefit — how will G-d hear his prayer to give him what he asks and thereby cause him eternal harm, G-d forbid? As in what is written: "There is wealth kept for its owner to his detriment" [Ecclesiastes 5:12]. And as is brought in the holy Zohar: "they prayed for wealth in this world — and afterwards it killed them", G-d forbid.

And therefore in truth the essential repair of prayer is through gazing at the true purpose in truth — and knowing and believing that everything is for the good. And then specifically one can pray afterwards for all that he needs. For then he can draw repairs from the light of the impression of the nullification toward the purpose — through which vessels will be made to draw through them His blessed abundant bounty and kindness in perfection with no lack of anything: livelihood and wealth and health — and health — children, life, and sustenance [banei, chayai, mezonai]. And even so — no harm and loss whatsoever will come to him through this, G-d forbid, in any direction — neither in this world nor in the World to Come. Rather, everything will be for eternal good as well. Since he has already repaired the vessels properly to receive through them the flow of kindness.

And therefore in truth no person knows how to pray in perfection — except the truly righteous Tzaddikim. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "One who has a sick person in his house — let him go to a sage and ask him to pray for mercy." And other people must bind their prayer to the Tzaddikim aforementioned — and they will elevate their prayer as is proper — to draw for them the flow of what they need: children, life, and sustenance, etc. In a manner that it will not harm them eternally, G-d forbid. Rather, on the contrary — through the flow specifically they will be repaired and return to G-d.

And therefore in truth there are many wonders and hidden matters in this matter of prayer. And therefore in truth it is forbidden to be stubborn and to press oneself about anything in one's prayer — as is explained elsewhere. For perhaps in truth it is impossible to fulfill one's request even through prayer — as it may harm him more, G-d forbid, if his request is fulfilled. And if he presses and is very stubborn in his prayer — it could be that he will accomplish with G-d the fulfillment of his request. For a person has great power to accomplish through his prayer. But it will not be for his benefit, G-d forbid. For he has not yet merited through his prayer to repair the vessel in perfection that is needed for receiving the flow that he wants. It is thus found: that as long as he is not praying for his needs — all the lacks he has are a great goodness for him. But through prayer he repairs vessels properly — through which he can — [can] — receive the flow of kindness to fill all the lacks — and it will not — [not] — harm him at all eternally either. And all of this — through gazing in truth at the purpose — which is entirely good as above.

And therefore in truth the essential prayer must truly be for one's eternal purpose. And this is the aspect of what is brought in the sacred books: that the essential prayer must be for the sake of completing the lack of the Shechinah, as it were. And therefore even the prayer one prays for one's physical needs — one should pray that G-d give him all his needs in a manner that will bring him eternal success. And this is the aspect of the order of the Shemoneh Esreh [Amidah] that our Sages of blessed memory arranged for us. And we begin first with the praise of the Omnipresent — in the first three blessings. And in the first blessing we mention how He, blessed be He, bestows good kindnesses — and all that He does is entirely for the good. And He is the King, helper, savior, and shield. And afterwards in the blessing of mechayeh hamaisim [Who revives the dead] — one includes also all other salvations and sustenance and healing. And one includes them many times together with the matter of the revival of the dead. That is, we praise and give thanks to G-d that all that He does with us is for our eternal benefit — which is the aspect of the revival of the dead. And only for this does He cause wondrous salvations to sprout for us at all times also in the physical: in matters of sustenance and healing and the like. All in a manner that will bring eternal success — also after the Revival. And thus it is understood that also what sometimes delays the flow, G-d forbid — all of it is for our eternal benefit after the Revival. For since G-d is so good and so beneficent and so all-powerful — and does kindness with the entire world at all times — sustains the living, etc. — if so, from where does it come that sometimes the flow is delayed? Certainly one must believe that it is only for eternal benefit. And therefore there the blessing mentions the matter of the Revival of the Dead many times in close proximity to the matter of sustenance. For in the matter of sustenance, a person's heart is most vexed — and it is hardest for him every time on account of the delay in livelihood. And therefore one must especially be reminded in this matter — that all the sustenance and provision that G-d provides for a person — all of it is for his eternal benefit after the Revival of the Dead. And for this very same reason the sustenance is sometimes delayed — for his eternal benefit afterwards.

And afterwards one says Kedushah and the blessing Atah Kadosh [You are holy] — which is the aspect of the very essence of the purpose: that all of Israel should merit after the Revival to sanctify His Name together with all the holy ones who will praise Him forever. And after having arranged the praise of the Omnipresent and proclaimed that all that G-d does is entirely for the good — then one prays for his needs. And even this one begins with the most essential: for knowledge and repentance and forgiveness of sin. And then one prays for the needs of the body. But all our intention even in this is only for the eternal purpose. For we know and acknowledge that G-d is all-powerful — and all that He does with us is entirely for the good. Only even so it is His blessed will that we pray before Him for our needs — in order to make vessels to receive the flow in perfection. And the essential thing — only for the sake of the eternal purpose. And therefore we recite the Kriyas Shma before the prayer. For through the Kriyas Shma we are encompassed in the One. And then specifically one can pray — as mentioned above.

One must strengthen oneself greatly in complete faith — to believe in himself that he has the power to accomplish anything through his prayer. For there are many types of weakness of mind in a person's heart in this matter — as every person knows within himself. And the majority of people imagine that they have no power for this. And therefore they do not strengthen themselves in prayer. And therefore one must toil with very great toil and service to strengthen himself to pray with intention. And the essential toil is at the beginning — that is, at the time he begins to strengthen himself to pray with intention — in the aspect of: "all beginnings are difficult." For at that time he has not yet seen any action from his prayer. But when he merits to overpower himself with all his strength to pray with intention — until he merits to accomplish some thing through his prayer — such as he prayed about some matter and was answered — then he is strengthened in this to believe even in himself that he has the power to accomplish through his prayer. Since he sees that G-d has already heard his prayer too and he was answered. And then a complete vessel is formed for him to receive the flow through the words of prayer. For the essential formation of the vessel is through faith — that is, through believing even in himself that G-d hears his prayer.

There are two kinds of kelipos [husks] that confuse a person's mind from strengthening himself in prayer. They are the husks of Eisav and Yishmo'el — which are the husks of the orlah [foreskin] and the peri'ah [secondary membrane]. The husk of Eisav-Amalek is the aspect of the outright orlah — for he denies the very foundation and does not acknowledge prayer at all. And he misleads a person's heart to say that prayer accomplishes nothing, G-d forbid — since the exile drags on for so long and every day one cries out and is not saved. And through the commandment of circumcision [bris milah] — which cuts the orlah that covers the bris — through this his evil husk is nullified and the aspect of the repair of the bris is drawn. Through which one merits to always strengthen himself in prayer. For the essential repair of prayer is through the repair of the bris.

But there is still another husk — the husk of the skin of peri'ah — which is the aspect of the husk of Yishmo'el. From which a different error is drawn in a person's heart — to become lax in prayer, G-d forbid. Because it seems to him that G-d has certainly already heard his prayer. Especially when he sees some sprouting of a ray of salvation — then it seems to him that his prayer has already been received. And he becomes lax about praying further. And this is drawn from the aspect of the husk of Yishmo'el — who is named thus from: "For G-d has heard your affliction" [Genesis 16:11] — and its Targum: "for G-d has received your prayer."

But in truth — even when one has not yet seen any salvation — one must believe that no prayer is in vain, G-d forbid. And to strengthen oneself in prayer even more. And likewise the reverse — even when one sees some salvation — it is forbidden to nullify and become lax in one's prayer because of this. Rather, one must rejoice in the salvation and give thanks for the past — and cry out for the future. For we still need many, very many salvations all the days of our lives — until we merit to come to what we need to come to — for which purpose we came into this world. And if one becomes lax in prayer because it seems to him that he has already accomplished much through his prayer — which is drawn from the aspect of the husk of Yishmo'el, the husk of peri'ah — through this, G-d forbid, the completion of his salvation is delayed and his exile is prolonged, G-d forbid. And then the husk of Eisav-Amalek — which is the husk of orlah — returns and arouses — and darkens his heart entirely from strengthening himself in his prayer through this very thing: that he sees that he has been crying out for so long and still is not answered with complete salvation.

And this is the aspect of: "one who was circumcised but did not perform peri'ah — it is as if he was not circumcised." And this is the aspect of: "And Mordechai returned" [Esther 6:12] — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: he returned to his sackcloth and his fast [Megillah 16a]. For even though he had already seen such a wondrous salvation — that they had made him ride upon the king's horse and proclaimed before him, etc. — even so, he did not become lax through this in his prayer and his crying out. And likewise regarding Esther it is written: "And Esther spoke further before the king, etc. — and she wept and implored him to remove the evil of Haman, etc." [Esther 8:3]. And this alludes to all of Kneses Yisroel [the Congregation of Israel] — who are the aspect of Esther. That even when they see great salvations and wondrous miracles — that the sitra achra in the aspect of Haman-Amalek has already fallen greatly, and they have hung him and his sons — [and his sons] — on the tree — even so they are not satisfied with this and still stand and pray and weep and implore before Him, blessed be He — like a child who wheedles before his father — to remove the evil of Haman who is the sitra achra entirely. So that they merit to be purified and sanctified entirely.

For even though certainly one must give much thanks for the salvations that have already been done for him — even so, we still need to greatly multiply prayer. For we still need many salvations all the days of our lives. Therefore one must strengthen oneself to always greatly multiply prayer.

Tefillin are written on the skin of an animal [ohr beheimah] — this is the aspect of people who are as learned as a person [adom] yet make themselves like an animal [beheimah]. That is, one must make himself like an animal — to set aside one's mind entirely, as if one has no mind at all — and rely only on faith. And then through this one's mind is clarified and the crookedness [akmimusin] in one's heart is straightened. For when a person sees that he has crookedness in his heart — especially when he has, G-d forbid, much crookedness in his heart — then he must set aside his mind entirely as if he has no mind at all — and go only in wholeness [temimus] and simplicity [peshitus] alone. And then he merits afterwards to great knowledge [da'as] and to straighten out the crookedness in his heart. And all of this is the aspect of tefillin.

Our Sages of blessed memory said: "Every single day a person's yetzer hara overpowers him — and were it not for the Holy One, blessed be He, helping him — he could not prevail against it" [Kiddushin 30b]. "Every single day the yetzer hara overpowers him" — this derives from the aspect of: "At first the thought arose to create the world with the attribute of strict judgment [midas hadin]". For this judgment arouses itself every single day — and wishes, G-d forbid, to conduct the world in this aspect. And from there the yetzer hara is aroused and intensifies — drawing from there every single day. For the essential yetzer hara and sitra achra derives from the aspect of judgments — drawn from the beginning of the contraction of the vacated space [chalal hapanui]. But G-d immediately has compassion and precedes the attribute of mercy before the attribute of judgment — as our Sages of blessed memory said: "He saw that the world could not endure [through judgment alone], etc." Which is the aspect of the help and assistance He provides the person every single day to shatter the yetzer hara — which is from the attribute of judgment. And this is the aspect of the tefillin of Rashi — where the kindnesses [chassadim] precede the strengths [gevuros]. And this is the aspect of: "He preceded the attribute of mercy and paired it with the attribute of judgment" — which is the essential governance and sustaining of the entire world. And therefore the essential tefillin that everyone wears are those of Rashi — for this is the essential governance and sustaining of the world through this aspect.

But there are Tzaddikim who are so great that they need no assistance from Above. And G-d conducts Himself with them as in the original thought — that is, through the attribute of strict judgment. And they stand firm through all the trials and sufferings and afflictions that derive from the attribute of judgment aforementioned. And they remain standing. And they sweeten the judgment at its very root — at the original thought. For they believe and know that the judgments and the sufferings themselves are great goodnesses. And through this they truly merit to ascend and be encompassed in the original thought — which is the aspect of: "Thus arose in thought" [kach alah b'machshavah] — said regarding the death of Rabbi Akiva. And this is the aspect of the tefillin of Rabbainu Tam — which are the aspect of the highest expanded consciousness [moichin govohim biyas]. And there the strengths precede the kindnesses. Which is the aspect of the governance that arose in the original thought — the aspect of the governance of the high Tzaddikim aforementioned.

And therefore one who wishes to draw close to G-d — to draw upon himself additional holiness — must also lay the tefillin of Rabbainu Tam. For all the distancing from G-d derives from the yetzer hara — whose root is from the attribute of judgment — drawn from the beginning of the contraction of the vacated space. And therefore the essential additional holiness is drawn upon a person through the tefillin of Rabbainu Tam — which are drawn from the aspect of the Tzaddikim aforementioned who ascend to the root of the judgment and sweeten everything at their root. Through which the power is drawn upon all the distant ones — to shatter and nullify the yetzer hara that is drawn from there.

Now — in the footsteps of the Mashiach, at the end of the exile — when the exile and the baal davar and the sitra achra intensify greatly — and the essential [intensification] is that heresy [apikorsus] has spread and is spreading greatly in the world — all of this intensification is the aspect of the birth-pangs [chevlei leida] — the birth-pangs of the Mashiach. For all of this derives from the root of the judgment of the aspect of the vacated space aforementioned. And therefore there is now no power to stand against them — except through the power of the very great Tzaddikim aforementioned: who can enter there — into the aspect of the vacated space — and sweeten the judgment at its very root. Through which the entire power of the yetzer hara of all who come into the world — drawn from there — is nullified. Therefore every person must be careful to lay the tefillin of Rabbainu Tam — which are drawn from the aspect of the high expanded consciousness of those Tzaddikim aforementioned. In order to receive power from them — to shatter the yetzer hara that has now greatly intensified — drawn from there.

Sometimes when a person rebukes himself or his fellow and begins to recall the evil deeds that were done — it is common for him to fall even more and more. For he falls greatly in his mind. And there are those who have fallen greatly through this. And all of this derives from the aspect of rebuke that is not as it should be — which weakens the power of the soul through arousing the foul odor of sins. For the essential rebuke must be in the aspect of tilting toward kindness [mateh k'lapei chesed]: to seek and to find in oneself — and likewise in one's fellow — at the very least some good points. And the rebuke should be in the manner of kindness — to strengthen oneself and one's fellow in G-d — and to trust in His immense compassion. For He has such kindness — that even all the evil deeds can be transformed into merits. Even if one has greatly multiplied transgression, G-d forbid. For "with G-d is kindness, and with Him is abundant redemption, etc." And the essential rebuke should be in a manner that one strengthens himself and his fellow to awaken toward G-d — and to begin to draw close to Him from now on. And not that through his rebuke he causes even more ruin — that the person falls even more, G-d forbid. And for such rebuke one can only merit through binding oneself to the Tzaddikim of the generation — who are the aspect of Moshe. Through whose rebuke [the rebuke of such Tzaddikim] they add and bestow a good fragrance upon the souls.

The essential obligation to speak with one's fellow in fear of Heaven — and to illuminate within him the true divine knowledge — is only for the sake of broadening one's fellow's mind. For the essential [goal] is to bring out oneself and one's fellow from the aspect of moichin d'katnus [smallness of mind] to the aspect of moichin d'gadlus [greatness of mind]. That is, to strive that the mind should grow and expand more and more every single time. Which is the aspect of the broadening of the boundary of the Land of Israel — the aspect of: "And I will enlarge your boundary" [Exodus 34:24]. And therefore each person who engages in this — to speak with his fellow about the true holy knowledge — must every single time be careful to make a boundary [seyag] for his words and to be silent where one must be silent. So as not to demolish one's fellow's boundary entirely. For this is the aspect of the prohibition of encroachment [hasogos gevul]. For not only does he not strive to broaden his fellow's boundary — but he also oppresses him more and enters into his boundary. For every single person of Israel has a boundary for himself in his own mind — to attain and understand up to that very boundary — in the aspect of: "And you shall ascend — you and Aharon, etc." [Exodus 19:24] — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: "you to your half and Aharon to his half, etc."

And therefore even though certainly it is a great commandment to speak with one's fellow every single time in fear of Heaven — and to have compassion upon him and to bring him out from his sins and corruptions — even so, one must be very careful that the engagement be for the good and not for harm — to repair and not to cause more ruin, G-d forbid. Not to look too much at one's fellow's disgrace and his deficiencies. For most of the quarrels and disputes and causeless hatred derive only from this: that each person looks at his fellow not with a favorable eye — and seeks to find in him only the blemishes and evil character traits — until it seems to him that it is impossible to bear them. And naturally likewise his fellow also looks at him in the same reverse manner — for "as water reflects the face, etc." [Proverbs 27:19]. Until causeless hatred and quarrels are stirred between them. Until through this our Temple was destroyed — [was destroyed] — and the exile was prolonged over us. And all of it only on account of — [on account of] — causeless hatred. As our Sages of blessed memory said. And all of this comes only from looking too much at one's fellow.

For in truth one must judge every person to the scale of merit. For even though certainly one must speak with him and illuminate his mind and bring him out from what he needs to be brought out from — and all of this is the aspect of judgment and law [din u'mishpot] — as explained in the inner teachings — even so, one must overpower oneself with compassion to enter with one's fellow beyond the letter of the law [lifnim mishuras hadin]. Not to look at him for bad — only for good — [for good] — and to judge him to the scale of merit always. So that one can speak with him. And as is explained elsewhere — that this is the aspect of the commandment: "And you shall do what is right and good" [Deuteronomy 6:18]. From which our Sages of blessed memory derived [the obligation] to go beyond the letter of the law. And they also derived from this the law of bar metzra [the neighbor's right of first refusal] — which is the aspect of the commandment to strive to broaden one's fellow's boundary. And both are one.

One who is on the lowest level — he must specifically find merit in himself — so as not to fall entirely, G-d forbid. And the essential purification and repentance of such a person is specifically through this. And this is the aspect of the purification of the parah adumah [the red heifer].

The essential teshuvah is to return from pride — from which come all the sins, G-d forbid. And to humble oneself and feel one's lowliness and insignificance in truth. For the essential teshuvah is the submission and the lowliness and a broken heart before G-d. Through this He forgives him for all the sins — and all the judgments are nullified from him.

Our Sages of blessed memory said that for the severe sin of wasting seed, G-d protect us — teshuvah is not effective for it. And in truth this is fitting for it — as explained in the inner teachings. But in truth even so — there is nothing that stands before teshuvah. Only the essential repair is through the Tzadik of the generation — as is explained in the inner teachings.

There is nothing that stands before teshuvah. And even for the blemish of drops of the brain [tipei hamoi'ach] — about which our Sages of blessed memory said that teshuvah is not effective, as mentioned above — and likewise for those about whom the verse says: "All her returnees do not return, and they will not attain the paths of life" [Proverbs 2:19] — but in truth, truth is truth: teshuvah is effective for all sins. As we have already found many, many wicked people who blemished in drops of the brain, and denied the very foundation — and even so they were accepted — [accepted] — in teshuvah.

Only — since they blemished so greatly — therefore they must join themselves together and be tested and stand in this trial of the distancing. That is, it is written of them that teshuvah is not effective for them. And when a person is foolish and senseless and has no compassion upon himself — not to destroy his world, G-d forbid — then he finds an excuse and exemption for himself to distance himself from teshuvah. Since it has already been written of him that teshuvah is not effective for him, G-d forbid. But one who thinks in truth about his purpose — and has compassion upon himself and considers his ways — for even so what will become of him in the end, and what will he do on the day of reckoning? Then — the more he finds and sees that they distance him further — the more compassion he has upon himself and he cries out to G-d from ever deeper in the depths of the heart. Until G-d looks down and sees from Heaven. For even though it has already been written of him that he is not accepted in teshuvah — even so he cries out to G-d about this itself: that he has blemished so greatly that they distance him so greatly. And even though I know that it is fitting to distance me because of the greatness of my blemishes — and certainly all that our Sages of blessed memory said is true and firm — even so, I know and believe that there are kindnesses of G-d, and such great — [great] — compassion before G-d, that He can also draw us close with compassion and receive us in complete teshuvah. For even so, did our Sages of blessed memory not say themselves: "There is nothing that stands before teshuvah."

And then — when one merits to stand in this trial of the distancing, and even so returns in complete teshuvah — then G-d has compassion upon him and he draws close through this specifically — through having stood in this trial of the distancing. And this is the aspect of: the distancing is the ultimate purpose of the drawing close.

The essential of all the blemishes of all the sins is in the aspect of the twenty-two letters. For one draws, G-d forbid, the letters that are in that thing which passes over him — to a place that draws them toward the sitra achra, etc., G-d protect us. For the essential vitality of all things is the letters within them — as is known. And therefore the essential repair is through speech — in the aspect of: "Take with you words and return to G-d" [Hosea 14:3]. And our Sages of blessed memory said: "He asks of you nothing but words." That is, one should multiply speaking holy words of cries and supplications and requests and songs and praises to Him, blessed be He. Until all the letters will be joined and repaired for good. And certainly this is a great and easy counsel — that everyone can fulfill. For one can merit teshuvah and the life of the World to Come through speech alone. Even if one does not merit to toil and labor in his service like the Tzaddikim and the upright who preceded us — who toiled and labored very, very greatly in many fasts and harsh and enormous mortifications. And even if, G-d forbid, what passes over him still passes over him — even so, if he does not allow himself to ever fall — and strengthens himself to speak words at the very least always before G-d — with cries and many supplications and requests to G-d — certainly in the end he will return to G-d.

But the baal davar intensifies against a person to prevent him — [to prevent him] — even from this. And the essential [obstruction] is through the entanglement of livelihood — through which one does not engage fully even in this easy counsel to return to G-d through holy speech. And therefore one must remind himself every single time of the truth — that "it is not through strength that a man prevails" [I Samuel 2:9]. And livelihood does not derive — [derive] — through one's toil and labor alone — but everything comes through the kindness of G-d and His salvation. And worries and entanglements do not help at all for livelihood — on the contrary, they damage livelihood greatly. And therefore even a craftsman or businessman can find himself some hours in the day to engage in the recitation of Psalms and hisbodidus, etc. And through this he will certainly return to G-d for the life of the World to Come.

Every person must strive greatly to seek and search after the lost things [avaidoas] all the days of his life. For this is the entire purpose of a person — who was created only for this: to seek after the lost things. Which are the aspect of the fallen sparks [nitzotzos hanefilim] — that are the aspect of things lost and cast away — that every person must strive greatly to seek and search after them all the days of his life. And especially if one has already sinned and blemished according to however he has blemished — especially the blemish of the bris, G-d forbid — through which he has now lost many more things himself. And one must search and seek after them greatly. And when one searches and seeks well — certainly he will find. For: "I toiled and did not find — do not believe" [Megillah 6b].

And this is the essential teshuvah for sins — as it is written: "And you will return to G-d, etc. — even if your scattered ones are at the very end of the heavens — from there He will gather you, etc." [Deuteronomy 30:2–4]. And it is written: "And you will seek from there G-d your G-d and you will find, etc." [Deuteronomy 4:29]. For one must greatly seek and search after the paths of holiness. For all the distance a person is from G-d is on account of the aforementioned lost things — through which he goes and wanders like a lost sheep and cannot find the path of life. And therefore a person must strive greatly all his days to seek and search after his lost things. For this is the essential teshuvah as above. And if one searches and seeks well — certainly he will find all that is needed for the repair of his soul. And even at the time when he does not yet merit to find — even so, through every toil and searching he has already found much. For no toil and searching is ever lost at all. And certainly one has already found much through every single word and through every toil and searching. For lais re'usa tava d'is'avad [no good intention is ever lost]. And even if one sees nothing of what he has found — and it appears to him that he has still not found anything and he is still far from G-d as before — even so, one must believe with complete faith that certainly one has found much through the toil itself. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "I toiled and found — believe" [Megillah 6b] — believe — [believe] — specifically. Even though one does not yet see what he found.

The essential teshuvah of every person is to return every single time from the evil thoughts in which he has been caught — to holy thoughts. In the aspect of: "Let the wicked abandon his way, and the man of iniquity his thoughts, and let him return to G-d" [Isaiah 55:7]. And this is the essential teshuvah: to return in one's thought from wherever one is — to holy thoughts. And even if one has gone astray in his thought however he has gone astray — even so, one must believe that in every way he disconnects himself in his thought from bad to good — it is precious in the eyes of G-d. For "He knows our formation, etc." [Psalms 103:14]. And the essential yetzer hara is the thoughts — as explained in the inner teachings.

The matter of what is explained in the holy Zohar — that for the blemish of the bris, teshuvah is not effective. And yet it is explained in the sacred books that even for this teshuvah is effective. But the essential repair is: to cast aside one's own understanding entirely and to strengthen oneself in complete faith, etc.

The essential of all blemishes and sins, G-d protect us, derives from the aspect of theft [gezail] — that is, from the fact that a person presses the moment [dochek es hasha'ah]. Which is the aspect of theft — as explained in the inner teachings. For the yetzer hara is only present for its hour. And if a person stands firm in the trial for a small amount of time — then afterwards the yetzer hara is automatically nullified and departs from him. And therefore the essential repair of teshuvah is drawn through the great Tzaddikim who press the moment not at all — even in their prayer. And they pray only with compassion and supplication. Also these Tzaddikim do not use their powerful staff [mateh az] — except for the sake of subduing the evil within the congregation [edah]. And through this Israel merits teshuvah. Also because the essential distancing from teshuvah is through people who obstruct [mone'im]. For people are sometimes very great obstructors — more than the yetzer hara itself. That is, through their controversy and their mockery and the like — as explained in the inner teachings. And therefore through the truly righteous Tzaddikim who draw their Torah innovations in completeness of all the repairs — through this they receive power to punish the obstructors or at least to silence them. Through this the awakening of teshuvah is drawn in the world.

There is one who has blemished and sinned so greatly — until he is in the aspect of one who has robbed the multitude [gazal es harabbim]. Whose blemishes affect all of Israel, G-d forbid. And then his entire repair is to engage in the needs of the multitude [tzorchei rabbim] — as our Sages of blessed memory said: "One who robbed the multitude — let him do from it the needs of the multitude." And the essential needs of the multitude are to cause them to merit the eternal purpose. And the essential [means] is to strive to have a share in drawing the Torah innovations of the truly righteous Tzaddikim — through which all the repairs are drawn in completeness. Through which the essential drawing of the repair of teshuvah for all of Israel comes — as above. And one must strive greatly that they spread in the world — whether through supporting with money those who engage in this, whether in person, whether through other aspects. For every single person can merit to have a share in this. And through this he will cause the multitude to merit — in the aspect of the needs of the multitude. And this is the essential repair for all his blemishes — which are the aspect of one who robbed the multitude as above.

What is brought in the holy Zohar — that for the blemish of the bris, teshuvah is not effective — but even so, through complete faith in the sages, even this sin can be repaired through the power of the holy Torah, which draws sweetening from the aspect of the supernal wisdom [chochmah ila'ah].

When a person sees that he has crookedness in his heart — especially when he has, G-d forbid, much crookedness in his heart — then he must make himself like an animal and set aside his mind entirely — as if he has no mind at all. And rely only on faith. And go only in temimus [wholeness] and peshitus [simplicity] alone. And then he merits afterwards to great da'as — the aspect of the expanded consciousness [moichin] of tefillin.

All the crookedness in the heart of many people — who say that they are unable to engage in the service of G-d because of deficiency of livelihood and other sufferings and obstacles, G-d forbid — all of this derives from the aspect of the confusion of the question of tzadik v'ra lo, rasha v'tov lo [why the righteous suffer and the wicked prosper]. For this confusion confuses many people. And even one who does not enter this question into his thought at all — even so, all of — [all of] — the aforementioned words derive and flow from there. And the essential repair for this is only temimus and simplicity: to cast aside all the wisdoms — and not to contemplate at all regarding His ways, blessed be He. And to know and believe — and believe — that "the ways of G-d are straight" [Hosea 14:10]. And to overpower oneself in all that passes over him — to seize some good each day — as much as possible. For lais yoma d'lais bei tava [there is no day that does not have good in it]. And to not deliberate at all regarding His blessed judgments. For this is the essential faith: to believe that everything is from G-d — and not to contemplate at all regarding Him. For He is righteous and upright. And through this itself one sweetens the judgments. And merits to draw close — [to draw close] — to G-d specifically through all that passes over him.

Every person must look into his own soul — that he not depart from the ways of true temimus. And to search his ways at all times. And to guard his soul very much — that the baal davar should not divert him from the truth, G-d forbid, through the futile wisdoms that are so common now in our many sins. And that he not invert truth to falsehood and transgression to commandment for him, G-d forbid. For this is the worst of all, G-d forbid. And he should remind himself at all times — that he is not pure in the matter of the desire for sexual union. And through this — the vessels — [the vessels] — of his brain are not in perfection. And even if he is established and known as a great scholar and pious person — even so, since he knows within his own soul that he is not pure and clear in this matter in full perfection as is proper — and therefore his grasp of the mind is not in perfection — therefore immediately when the baal davar wishes to divert him from the path of true temimus even by a single point — even though it seems to him that the Torah mandates such — he must fear for his soul and consider: perhaps — [perhaps] — he is erring in the matter. And this thought and view derives in him from the aspect of: "if he has not merited — it becomes for him a deadly poison", G-d protect us — said of one who has not yet merited the perfection of the vessels of the brain through the repair of the bris in perfection. Therefore — he — [he] — must be especially careful not to mislead himself and not to invert the words of the living G-d, G-d forbid.

And he must be especially, especially careful in this matter regarding controversy. As we have already seen many souls who went down to the pit alive, G-d protect us, through having multiplied controversy against the upright because of the error of their mind — and it seemed to them that their intention was for the sake of Heaven. As is explained in the inner teachings. And also for himself alone in the service of G-d — one must also cry out and wail greatly to G-d, that He lead him in the straight and true path always. Perhaps he will merit to draw close to G-d as is proper. And as King David cried out much about this — as explained in the inner teachings. For one needs a very great merit and a very great salvation and very great compassion — and great striving and great toil all the days of his life — to merit to weigh out his ways in truth at every time and to walk in the holy path truly and truthfully and not deviate right or left. And not to mislead himself in any matter, G-d forbid — on account of the imperfection of the vessels of his brain. But at the very least — when one guards himself from deviating at the very least from the ways of temimus — then he is at least certainly protected from utter stumbling, G-d forbid. For "he who walks in wholeness walks securely" [Proverbs 10:9].

Every person who feels in himself that he is not holy as is proper — must humble and nullify himself before G-d. And not wish to go in matters too great and too wondrous for him [gedolos u'niflo'os mimenu] — to draw upon himself the aspect of the holy spirit, the spirit of prophecy. Since he knows that he is far from this. And if he wishes to draw upon himself the aspect of visions and sights — he can cause himself even more and more ruin. As very many have stumbled in this. Rather, he must go in temimus and beseech G-d to be in his aid — to emerge from his insignificance. And to merit to sanctify himself as is proper. And then — if he merits and is worthy of receiving the holy spirit, through the path of holiness, in perfection — G-d who is good will do with him as He wills.

In truth there is no person who does not have his hour [sha'ah]. But many lose their hour — in which they could have succeeded physically and spiritually — through their futile wisdoms. Through pressing the moment [dochek es hasha'ah]. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "Whoever presses the moment — the moment presses him." For G-d fulfills: "with the wholesome You act wholesomely, and with the crooked You act crookedly" [Psalms 18:27]. And since he is crooked and wishes G-d to immediately fulfill his desire — and when he does not have what he desires, he says that it is impossible in this way to serve G-d — it is thus found that he is crooked and deliberates regarding His blessed attributes. And then G-d also acts crookedly with him — and the moment presses him.

But one who goes in temimus and truly believes that G-d is certainly righteous and upright — and that the sufferings and hardship he endures are all for the good — for his hour has not yet come. And fulfills: "It is good to wait in silence for the salvation of G-d" [Lamentations 3:26]. For sometimes G-d does not give the person the needs of his salvation immediately — until he multiplies prayer about this. For "G-d longs for the prayer of Israel." And also in prayer it is forbidden to press the moment — as explained elsewhere. And sometimes the salvation is delayed still for other reasons. And therefore one must go only in temimus — and believe in the uprightness of His blessed judgments — and always multiply prayer for everything. And then certainly the moment stands [favorably] for him. For certainly the hour of his salvation will come. And as is explained in the words of our Sages of blessed memory: "Whoever makes himself whole [mistemim] — the moment stands favorably for him, etc."

One who goes in temimus — he is the essential beloved child before G-d, as explained in the inner teachings. And one who goes after the futile wisdoms and cunning schemes [armimiyos] of vanity — which are like actual divinations [nachushim mamash], G-d protect us — he is the aspect of crooked and twisted [ikaish u'fsaltal]. And G-d fulfills with him: "with the crooked You act crookedly" [Psalms 18:27]. And he is the aspect of one with a blemish [ba'al mum] — which is the opposite of wholeness [temimus] — which is the language of completeness [shleimus].

The essential [means by which] G-d takes glory in Israel before all the nations is through their true ways of temimus. And this is the aspect of: "There are sixty queens, etc. — one is she, my dove, my perfect one [tamasi]" [Song of Songs 6:8–9] — specifically tamasi — the aspect of temimus.
Completed and finished. Praise to G-d, Creator of the world.
